entries.label: US political revolution
entries.summary: The US president's drive to remove checks on his power makes the United States the main source of global risk.
entries.quote: Trump is attempting to dismantle checks on his power, capture the machinery of government, and weaponize it against his enemies, making the United States the principal source of global risk in 2026.

entries.label: Overpowered
entries.summary: China's bet on electricity-based industry against the US bet on fossil fuels starts to show a winner.
entries.quote: China is betting on electrons. The United States is betting on molecules. This year, we'll start to see who was right.

entries.label: The Donroe Doctrine
entries.summary: Washington seeks direct control over the Western Hemisphere while stepping back from global policing.
entries.quote: The Trump administration doesn't want to be the world's policeman but intends to assert direct control over America's own backyard.

entries.label: Europe under siege
entries.summary: The political centre weakens in France, Germany and the UK at once, so Europe cannot fill the US security gap.
entries.quote: Europe's political center is collapsing in all three major powers at once, leaving the continent unable to fill the security vacuum left by America's retreat.

entries.label: Russia's second front
entries.summary: The main danger in Europe moves from the Ukraine front line to a hybrid conflict between Russia and NATO.
entries.quote: The most dangerous front in Europe will shift from the trenches in Donetsk to the hybrid war between Russia and NATO.

entries.label: State capitalism with American characteristics
entries.summary: The US government picks corporate winners and losers on an unusual scale.
entries.quote: The most economically interventionist American administration since the New Deal will pick winners and losers at a scale not seen in modern US history.

entries.label: China's deflation trap
entries.summary: China stays in deflation and pushes cheap exports onto world markets.
entries.quote: Beijing won't break out of its deflationary trap this year; instead, it will keep trying to export its way out, flooding global markets with cheap goods at everyone else's expense.

entries.label: AI eats its users
entries.summary: Revenue pressure pushes some AI firms toward extractive business models that threaten social stability.
entries.quote: Under pressure to generate revenue and justify sky-high valuations, some AI companies will adopt extractive business models that threaten social and political stability.

entries.label: Zombie USMCA
entries.summary: The North American trade pact survives but in a state of limbo.
entries.quote: North American trade will be stuck in limbo as USMCA staggers on, neither dead nor alive.

entries.label: The water weapon
entries.summary: Control of water becomes a weapon in several dangerous rivalries.
entries.quote: Water is becoming a loaded weapon in several of the world's most dangerous rivalries.

entries.label: 'Tariff man' at large
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects the US trade war not to keep escalating in 2026.
entries.quote: Donald Trump's trade war will keep escalating, causing more economic havoc in 2026. That's a common fear. We don't buy it.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Deglobalization
entries.summary: Eurasia Group does not expect 2026 to be a year of deglobalization.
entries.quote: But that doesn't mean 2026 will be a year of deglobalization.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Spheres of influence
entries.summary: Eurasia Group doubts that great powers will carve the world into spheres of influence.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Sell America
entries.summary: Eurasia Group rejects the fear of a broad investor flight from US assets.
entries.note: Only the heading is on the free page; the argument is in the gated report. Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

notes: Landing page lists labels and headline sentences. Full PDF is behind an email form (whitepaper.cfm?fileID=13327) and was not downloaded. The landing page says 2026 US-China conflict is itself a red herring, but the red-herrings page does not list it as a separate herring.
